newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria to boost oilfields capacity by 45,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Syria to boost oilfields capacity by 45,000 bpd.

text.p: Syria's al-Furat Petroleum Company (AFPC) said on Monday it is planning to expand the production capacity of its al-Thuban and Jarnouf oilfields by 45,000 barrels per day ((bpd) to 75,000 bpd.

The project at the AFPC's concession area of Dayr Azzawr, northeast of Damascus and near the Iraqi border, also includes the construction of a gas gathering system capable of handling 45 million cubic feet per day, it said.

Al-Furat, owned 50 percent by Syrian Petroleum Company (SPC), 15.625 percent by Shell unit Pecten, 15.625 percent by Syria Shell and 18.75 percent by Germany's Deminex, produced 450,000 bpd of light crude during the last few year.
But oil industry sources say production has recently fallen.
Syrian production totals around 600,000 bpd of light and heavy crude, of which around 330,000 bpd is exported.
The AFPC called contractors and companies interested in participating in the al-Thuban/Jarnouf project to apply for a pre-qualification contest before the tender which will be issued in October.
The call, published in official Syrian newspapers, set September 16 as the final date for applications for the pre-qualification contest.
Contractors who passed a similar pre-qualification contest for the development of the company's Omar, Maleh and Azrak fields are excluded from the new tender.
Al-Furat was formed in May 1985. The production-sharing agreement provides for a development period of 25 years, renewable for a further 10 years.
